(7) Item 7 - Selecting FX Bank Deal hides full Destination (To) Card and renders 'Destination (To) is not applicable for FX Bank Deal' notice; switching back to FX Crypto Conversion restores Destination card. (8) Item 8 - Selecting FX Bank Deal hides Client's Settlement upload section in Settlement Proofs, rendering 'Client's Settlement is not applicable for FX Bank Deal'. (9) Item 9 - Treasury Review dialog for a no-proof deal: confirm-deal-btn is disabled AND 'Settlement proofs required to confirm' amber message is visible; processor upload button remains enabled to allow attaching a proof to unlock Confirm. No critical or blocking defects found.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L902-909 reseed logic for transfer_types: deletes all and reinserts on every startup whenever either 'FX Crypto Conversion' or 'FX Bank Deal' is missing, but it runs delete_many on every restart in the affirmative path. Acceptable for a one-off migration; consider gating with a one-shot migration flag or upsert-by-name to preserve any admin edits to is_active or display names.

to_type/to_company/to_bank/to_account_num are now Optional but server-side validation does NOT enforce that they MUST be empty when transfer_type='FX Bank Deal'. A trader could submit FX Bank Deal with a to_company filled and it would be persisted. Add server-side rule: if transfer_type=='FX Bank Deal' then to_* fields are coerced to empty strings (or 422).

Same applies to Client's Settlement proofs for FX Bank Deal - frontend hides the UI, but a crafted POST could still attach client proofs. Backend should drop/ignore client_proofs when transfer_type=='FX Bank Deal'.

NewDealPage.jsx and EditDealPage.jsx duplicate the divide/multiply formula and conditional rendering for isFxBankDeal/isDivideMode. Extract to a shared hook (useDealFormulas) so future formula changes do not require parallel edits in two files.

Treasury Confirm-disabled-when-0-proofs is correct, but the disable condition `(clientProofs.length + processorProofs.length) === 0` does not distinguish FX Bank Deal (which has no client proofs by design). For an FX Bank Deal a single processor proof unlocks Confirm - intended, but worth documenting in code comment to avoid future regression.

DealsPage list table now exposes history[] for every row. For deals with long histories this inflates the list payload. Backend already projects 'history':1 on the list endpoint - consider truncating to last 3 entries server-side for the list response and returning the full array only on the detail GET.
